chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Abd al-A'la, the freedman of the family of Sam, who said:

I faced Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in some of the streets of the city on a summer day of intense heat, and I said: 'May I be your ransom, what is your status with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and your proximity to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), while you are exhausting yourself on a day like this?' He said: 'O Abd al-A'la, I went out seeking sustenance so that I might become independent of people like you.'

key_terms.عَنْ مِثْلِكَ: from people like you (referring to others)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq work in the heat of summer despite his high status?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) embodiment of *istighna* (self-sufficiency), demonstrating that even the Ahl al-Bayt, despite their spiritual rank, engaged in manual labor to avoid depending on the wealth of others. It serves as a practical model for Shia jurisprudence regarding the permissibility and virtue of earning a lawful livelihood through one's own effort, countering any notion that religious leaders should be exempt from worldly work.
